doc.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012

title: The 1987 Ace award acceptance speech for History of Jazz
summary: Crohn tells how he won a cable Ace award as writer of the History of Jazz series and recounts the speech thanking jazz itself.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: So in 1987 I won an Ace award which is the cable equivalent of an Emmy. Back then they had Emmys for broadcast television, and the Ace for cable television. A couple of years later they merged and became the same thing, but it was the same thing. The crowded theater in Hollywood, the searchlights outside, tuxedos, you know. And so I won it as a writer for my “History of Jazz” series, before Ken Burns, and so what I said was — I practiced this — was that I thanked all the people you’re supposed to thank — David Chertok, the film collector, Wynton Marsalis, Chick Corea, Branford — good move Monk.
You want to start that story again?

Yeah. So real quick I’ll sum up. Back then the Ace awards were for cable and Emmys were for broadcast television, because they merged them. It was the same type of ceremony, broadcast on HBO. Searchlights, tuxedos, crowded theater everything. And I won it as a writer. And I was very nervous and I’d rehearsed an acceptance speech. And I got up in front of the crowd. The first thing I said is this is the wrong side of a camera for a writer to be on. But then I thanked all the people, David Chertok, the film collector, Branford Marsalis, Wynton Marsalis, Chick Corea and the people I work with. And then I said, “And I want to thank jazz itself, born in the U.S.A. a hundred years ago, and re- born every time someone takes a solo.”
